events.title: HAM-DEFCON
events.description: HAM-DEFCON is a cybersecurity competition organized by HAM-ARC club of National Institute Of Technology Warangal Telangana, India. Event Details: Format: Attack & Defense Categories: Web Exploitation, Binary Exploitation (Pwn), Reverse Engineering, Cryptography, and Infrastructure Hardening. Team Size: 1–4 Members Categories: Web Security, Binary Exploitation (Pwn), Reverse Engineering, Applied Cryptography, and Service Hardening Rules & Code of Conduct On-Site & Network Access: The competition is strictly offline at the NIT Warangal campus. All team traffic and service interactions must route exclusively through the official network access gateway. Multi-Tiered Flagstores: Each service hosts multiple independent flagstores (Easy, Medium, Hard). Flags are dynamically rotated and refreshed every tick (round). Scoring Breakdown: Attack Points: Awarded for successfully exploiting opponent services and submitting their flags to the Flag Submission endpoint. Defense Points: Maintained by successfully patching vulnerabilities while keeping services operational. SLA (Uptime) Points: Awarded each round your services remain healthy, responsive, and passing all automated checker functionality tests. Scope & Infrastructure Immunity: Only designated opponent service ports and containers are in scope. Attacking the game engine, scoring backend, automated checkers, host hypervisors, or other teams’ network credentials will result in immediate disqualification. Fair Play & Service Integrity: Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks, network floods, deleting arbitrary system utilities, bricking service runtimes to prevent checker evaluation, and flag sharing or collusion between teams are strictly prohibited.
events.location: National Institute Of Technology Warangal, Hanamkonda, Telangana, India, 505004

events.title: StealthCup 2026
events.description: StealthCup is an evasion focused CTF and a research project by AIT, held this year at Hackfest in Quebec City. Most CTFs reward speed. StealthCup rewards staying invisible. Teams attack a live IT and OT enterprise range while a real SOC stack watches. The team that reaches its objectives with the fewest severe detections wins. Up to 12 teams compete, each playing an IT part and an OT part, for the overall cup plus separate IT and OT cups. Detections are shown in real time so teams can adapt their evasion strategy. Resets of infrastructure and scores are possible but cost points. Ideal team size is 4 to 8 players, with 2 to 4 on each side. The event is designed for professionals with a pentesting background, familiarity with evasion techniques, Windows and OT environments is an advantage. The event runs in English. Technical details and objectives are shared with confirmed teams a few days before the event. Attack paths and evasion tricks from the event feed into detection research. The 2025 results were published at ACM AsiaCCS 2026. Winners join the StealthCup Hall of Fame and are published on the website, participants can opt for anonymity. Registration: team registration at https://stealth.ait.ac.at/team-application/, individuals without a team at https://stealth.ait.ac.at/individual-registration/
events.location: On-site, Quebec City, Canada (Hackfest, Quebec City Convention Centre). Remote participation only on request.

events.title: EyesOpenCTF 7th edition
events.description: EyesOpenCTF 2026 is a FREE CTF competition organized as part of the 7th edition of EOCON. This year, the competition goes far beyond a traditional CTF. You are not simply joining to solve isolated challenges. You are entering The Convergence, a live 48-hour cyber adventure in which reality itself is beginning to fracture. Across more than 40 challenges and 8 disciplines, teams will investigate corrupted systems, recover hidden Reality Fragments, unlock classified dossiers, expose compromised actors, and gradually reconstruct the truth behind a phenomenon threatening the entire world. Every flag matters. Each solved challenge can reveal new intelligence, unlock characters and locations, alter the mission briefing, and move the story forward in real time. The competition platform becomes a living investigation that evolves with the progress of the Operators. Expect : - web exploitation, - digital forensics, - reverse engineering, - binary exploitation, - cryptography, - OSINT, - AI security, and more—woven into a single coherent mission unlike any previous EyesOpenCTF. Built for teams from around the world and open to different experience levels, EyesOpenCTF is both a proving ground and an immersive narrative experience where competitors can learn, compete, get noticed, and join a fast-growing international cybersecurity community. As part of EOCON, the competition also connects participants with experts, researchers, recruiters, entrepreneurs, and emerging talent from Africa and beyond. It is a place where technical ability meets storytelling, where discoveries change the mission, and where tomorrow’s collaborations, careers, and opportunities begin. Form your team. Enter the Protocol. Recover the Fragments. events.title: CyberSci Regional Qualifiers 2026-27
events.description: CyberSci is Canada's national Cyber Security Challenge for university and college students. - Think you've got an elite team of students? Come and prove it. Our winners will go on to compete against the best in the world. - Just starting out? This is the best way to learn and rise to the top. - Annual in-person events since 2016. (Online during Covid.) Over 500 students so far. Format: - Modified jeopardy style. Realistic IT environment. - Regional qualifiers are held in Nov-Dec each year. - National finals are the following July. - Winning teams represent Canada at international events in the Fall. For Regionals (qualifiers): We do hacking in the morning, interviews in the afternoon, and job offers by supper (for intern/summer/coop jobs). - Full-time job offers take a few more days. - Students register their team through their school instructor or computer club. Max 2 teams per school. For nationals: Participants will be the winning team from each regional/qualifier - PLUS one all-juniors (19 and under) - AND one all-women team (chosen from participants at the Regionals). Two-day event.
